name: jakarta-vo-1
text: Parts of this city sink up to twenty-five centimetres a year. [short pause] And it's not the sea rising... it's the ground falling. This is Jakarta. Almost forty-two million people... and about forty percent of the city already sits below sea level. So why is it sinking? [short pause] Here's the part most people don't know. Jakarta is pumping out its own foundations. Homes and factories pull water from wells under their own floors... the soft clay underneath dries out... and the city drops with it. Parts of North Jakarta sank two and a half metres in just ten years. Now the sea stops at a wall... higher than the streets behind it. So Indonesia's answer? [excited] Build a brand new capital. Nusantara... in Borneo, more than twelve hundred kilometres away. A forty-five billion dollar plan for over a million people. So far... about ten thousand have moved in. Fix the sinking city... or build a new one? Which would you pick?
